$comment: Every on-demand native gate, in one place. Read by build-logic (FeatureModules, the Play splits, settings includes, dynamicFeatures, native pins, proguard keeps, the core modules' jniLibs) and by native/gates.py for the shell side (collect-natives.sh, release.yml, build-fdroid-libs.sh). How to add a gate: docs/src/content/docs/development/architecture.md, 'Adding a native gate'.

gates.doc: `:feature:litert`: the LiteRT interpreter, shared by offline Whisper dictation (`:core:voice`) and the sticker editor's own background remover (`:core:content`).
`:feature:handwriting`: ML Kit's digital-ink recogniser.

`:feature:speech`: the whisper.cpp and Whistle native libraries behind the GGML Whisper models and Whistle (`:core:voice`), with whisper.cpp's OpenCL build for Adreno GPUs on arm64 (Compute on the Offline Whisper screen). Only the libraries move; their Kotlin stays in the base.

`:feature:opus`: libopus and the Ogg writer that compress dictation audio before it is uploaded to a transcription server (`OpusEncoder`, `:core:voice`). Its own gate, not the speech one: server dictation is the only user, and it should not have to fetch the on-device engines' libraries to get 300 KB of encoder. Until it is here the clip goes as WAV.

`:feature:executorch`: the app's ExecuTorch runtime (`libwmexecutorch`), shared by Asr4All, Parakeet and Moonshine dictation and the FUTO Swipe glide engine (`:core:voice`). Its own gate so that turning on the glide engine does not also fetch whisper.cpp and Whistle.

`:feature:onnx`: Microsoft's ONNX Runtime and the sherpa-onnx bridge built on it (`libwmsherpa`), behind the Sherpa voice engine (`:core:voice`). Outside Play the runtime is read straight out of Microsoft's AAR on Maven Central, never mirrored. Other ONNX models can ride the same runtime later; only sherpa-onnx's bridge is specific.

`:feature:kiwi`: the Kiwi morphological analyser behind Korean spacing correction (`:core:input`), upstream's prebuilt library, about 18 MB. Upstream builds for arm64 and x86-64 only, so armeabi-v7a holds an empty stand-in that bundletool's same-ABI rule asks for and KoreanSpacing never loads. Not built here from source, so not in F-Droid's build.

`:feature:webrtc`: the WebRTC library behind PairDrop in Send files (`:feature:ime`), about 12 MB per ABI and off until PairDrop is switched on. Its Java API stays in the base; only the library moves. A prebuilt binary, so not in F-Droid's build.
`:feature:grammar`: the Harper grammar library (`:core:intelligence`).
`:feature:spell`: the Hunspell library behind spell checking against an imported `.aff` and `.dic` (`:core:prediction`).
`:feature:ocr`: the Tesseract library behind the scanner's offline reads (`:core:intelligence`).
`:feature:rime`: librime, behind the optional RIME engine for Chinese (`:core:input`). The built-in composers need nothing from it.
`:feature:mozc`: Google's Mozc converter, behind the optional Mozc engine for Japanese (`:core:input`). Its dictionary is a separate download; the built-in Japanese composer needs neither.
`:feature:bergamot`: Mozilla's Bergamot translator behind the translate tool's free on-device engine (`:core:intelligence`). Only the library moves; the models are downloaded per language direction.
`:feature:ct2`: CTranslate2, the runtime of the translate tool's NLLB engine (`:core:intelligence`). Only the library moves; the model is a separate 630 MB download.
`:feature:zinnia`: zinnia, the offline recogniser behind Chinese and Japanese handwriting where ML Kit's is not in the build or not picked (`:core:intelligence`). Its models are separate downloads.

`:feature:llama`: llama.cpp, the on-device AI runtime for GGUF models (`:core:intelligence`), with libmtmd for vision models' projectors; the OpenCL build for Adreno GPUs is the `llamagpu` gate. LiteRT-LM, the default runtime, has its own gate (`LlmModule`); only a GGUF model asks for this one.

`:feature:llamagpu`: llama.cpp's OpenCL build for Adreno GPUs (`:core:intelligence`), a third arm64 libwmllama that a process loads instead of a CPU one when Compute is GPU on an Adreno phone. Its own gate so that nobody else downloads it; asked for by `LlamaCpp` and the Compute chips.
`:feature:docscan`: the built-in document scanner's library (OpenCV's core and imgproc, `:core:intelligence`), behind the scanner tool where Google's scanner is missing or switched off.
`:feature:zxing`: zxing-cpp's readers, behind the QR scanner where ML Kit's barcode reader is missing or not picked (`:core:intelligence`).

`:feature:imagegen`: the sticker generator's runtimes (`:core:intelligence`): MNN on the CPU (`libwmimagegen`, also the scanner's PaddleOCR runtime in builds without LiteRT, F-Droid's, the handwriting panel's PaddleOCR reader wherever ML Kit has no model, and the upscaler's in every build) and, arm64 only, the runner that drives Qualcomm AI Hub's Stable Diffusion on the NPU through the Qualcomm runtime (`libwmimagegen_qnn`, never built for F-Droid: it is compiled against Qualcomm's QNN headers). Only the libraries move; the models are separate downloads.

`:feature:npu`: the Qualcomm NPU runtime (LiteRT's dispatch library and the QNN libraries) behind Compute = NPU for on-device AI. Assets only, unpacked into app storage by `NpuRuntime` in :core:intelligence.

`:feature:googlehome`: the Google Home APIs SDK, Play builds only. Every other build either compiles it in or has no Google Home at all. No flag: the SDK unpacked under feature/ime/libs/googlehome is the decision.

ML Kit's bundled text recogniser and barcode reader behind the scanner tool. Never a Play module: Play builds use the play-services twins, whose models come from Play services. Only [NativeDelivery] backs it, on a build that leaves the two libraries out of the APK.
